transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Pelican Security), Marc Rivera (Pelican Infra), Becky Chen (Pelican Procurement)

--- Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect) ---
Walkthrough of SIG questionnaire items focusing on SOC2, encryption, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, data residency; next steps to provide evidence and diagrams.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood, AE. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. Today we wanted to walk through the SIG and call out where we can attach evidence and sample docs.
00:12 Aisha: Thanks Jordan, appreciate it. We just want to make sure the SOC 2 scope aligns and understand how audit logs and key management works. Also we'll need notes for procurement.
00:25 Jordan: Totally. Quick agenda: SOC 2 and compliance artifacts, SIG controls mapping, RBAC/SSO and SAML attributes, encryption and KMS, audit log retention and how to get samples, and data residency. We'll pause for questions along the way.
01:02 Priya: I'll start on the tech piece — sorry, small background, Redwood's hosted API plus dedicated/private deployment options. We support hosted, dedicated pools, and private VPC installs. The SIG has separate sections for control environment, access control, encryption, and vendor management.
01:25 Marc: Quick question — when you say private, do you mean full on-prem or VPC with private control plane? Which pieces live in our network?
01:35 Priya: Good question. We have two flavors: Private deployment is a customer-managed control plane in their VPC or an on-prem package for air-gapped setups. In the VPC case, compute still runs in your VPC and we provide the orchestration artifacts; for on-prem it's fully customer-managed. Sorry if I said 'dedicate' earlier, sometimes the name gets fuzzy in calls.
02:05 Aisha: And SOC 2 — do you scope both hosted and dedicated? We need the report to cover production data at rest and in transit.
02:12 Jordan: Our SOC 2 covers the hosted API environment and Redwood's control plane. For Dedicated and Private, we provide a SOC 2 carve-out and runbook and we sign the attestation language in contracts. We'll share the SOC 2 report pdf and SOC 2 scope matrix. Link will be in the follow-up.
02:45 Becky: Procurement will need the SIG export and any attestations for sub processors.
02:52 Jordan: Yes, we'll send the completed SIG, the CAIQ/ SIG-L export, a list of subprocessors, and the SOC 2 pdf.
03:10 Priya: Going into the SIG, control A.1 covers RBAC and SSO. We support SAML 2.0 SSO, SCIM provisioning for users, and granular RBAC — roles at org, project, and route levels. Small caveat: some RBAC features require Dedicated or Private in certain enterprise setups.
03:40 Marc: Which attributes do you require from our IdP? We need to map groups.
03:46 Priya: Typically we consume: nameid, email, groups, and optional department attribute. We can accept custom claim mappings. For SCIM, we support group sync.
04:05 Aisha: Is there an audit trail for SSO events? We need login events tied to user IDs.
04:10 Priya: Yes — we log authentication events, SAML assertion successes/failures, provisioning events. Those appear in the audit logs with timestamps, principal, IP, and action. We can share sample log snippets.
05:00 Jordan: On encryption — data in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3, at rest we use AES-256. For hosted customers, keys are KMS-managed; we support customer-managed keys via KMS in supported clouds. For Dedicated we offer BYOK options and HSM integrations in the private model.
05:28 Marc: Any nuance around ephemeral KV cache or KV "cash"? I saw a note referencing KV cache in your docs.
05:34 Priya: Ha, yes the transcript generator often says KV cash. We mean KV cache/key-value cache used for model inference. Sensitive data in KV cache is scoped — we don't persist user level plaintext long term and it's encrypted at rest.
06:00 Aisha: For KMS, do you support customer KMS in Azure and AWS? Any limitations?
06:06 Priya: We support AWS KMS and AWS CloudHSM for hosted customers and Dedicated; Azure Key Vault is supported for private deployments. There's a short compatibility matrix we'll send. Also rotating keys is supported with minimal downtime for crypto operations.
06:40 Becky: On evidence delivery — we usually require screenshots, config files, and a signed SOC report. Will you provide CSV exports for SIG?
06:46 Jordan: Yes, SIG export in machine-readable CSV plus a control mapping doc and the SOC 2. For some items we can attach sample logs and config snippets (sanitized).
07:20 Priya: Now audit logs — retention defaults are 90 days for hosted, configurable for Dedicated/Private. We support forwarding to your SIEM (S3, Splunk, Datadog) and can ship through a connector. Logs include request metadata, token usage, authorization checks, admin actions.
07:52 Marc: Is there a way to restrict who can download raw logs? We need RBAC on log access.
07:58 Priya: Yes — log access is controlled by RBAC. Only roles with audit_read or infra_admin can export logs. All exports are logged as events.
08:25 Aisha: For evidence, can you provide a sample of an audit log entry for a token revoke and a model rollout event?
08:33 Priya: Absolutely, we'll include two redacted entries: one token_revoke event, one model_rollout event.
09:05 Jordan: Data residency — Pelican mentioned EU regs. We have regional hosting in eu-central and eu-west, and we can pin data residency at the tenant level. For Dedicated/Private you can keep everything in your VPC.
09:35 Marc: If we go hosted but EU-resident, are backups replicated out of region?
09:40 Priya: Good callout. Backups for EU-resident hosted tenants remain in the EU. We do cross-region replication only if customer opts in and signs additional terms. We'll add that to the evidence doc.
10:10 Aisha: About retention — what about audit log retention for compliance? Can you retain beyond 365 days? We may need up to 7 years for some records.
10:20 Priya: For Hosted, default is 90 days but we offer extended retention as an add-on up to multi-year via archival to your S3 or our long-term storage with locked access controls. Dedicated/Private gives you full control.
10:55 Becky: On subprocessors, is there a list and how often is it updated? Procurement likes a living list.
11:02 Jordan: We maintain a subprocessors list and notify customers of changes per contract. We'll attach the current list and cadence.
11:30 Aisha: A couple of SIG-specific Qs: control around change management, configuration reviews — do you have formal change windows and approvals?
11:38 Priya: Yes — we have documented change-management processes, change approvals, and rollback runbooks. For Dedicated/Private customers we can include tailored runbooks in the customer evidence package.
12:10 Marc: Any network requirements we need to open? For VPC peering or private link?
12:18 Priya: For VPC setups we provide VPC templates and required ports. For Private with private control plane you may need a few inbound rule changes for administrative endpoints. We'll put that in the infra diagram.
12:50 Jordan: Ok quick recap before we go to next steps. Redwood will: send SIG CSV export, SOC 2 report link, subprocessors list, sample audit log entries, infra diagram, KMS compatibility matrix. Pelican will confirm data residency regions and provide list of stakeholders for evidence review.
13:12 Aisha: Sounds good. Also we'll need a statement on pen testing cadence and whether Redwood shares reports or summary findings.
13:20 Jordan: We do annual pen tests and can share a redacted summary and remediation status. Full reports are usually shared under NDA; we'll note that in the follow-up.
13:38 Becky: One administrative thing — can you put pricing impact if we need extended log retention and customer-managed KMS? Procurement needs a short note.
13:48 Jordan: Yes we'll add a short pricing note for extended retention and BYOK/HSM support.
14:10 Priya: I'll attach sample log lines and the model rollout event example. Also architecture diagram and the SAML attribute mapping example.
14:30 Marc: Thanks. Timeline — can we get the artifacts by Friday the 20th?
14:36 Jordan: Yes that's our target. We'll send initial packet by 2026-11-20.
15:00 Aisha: Great, thanks everyone.
15:05 Jordan: Thanks team, we'll follow up with the email and shared drive link.
15:12 Meeting end.
